metadata.name: checkwash
metadata.summary: Flags known patterns of weakened tests and CI checks in a Git diff.
metadata.description:
# checkwash [![CI](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/checkwash.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/checkwash/) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/LICENSE) **Check whether a code change weakens your tests.** A test can pass after it stops checking something useful. checkwash reads your Git diff and flags known patterns such as deleted assertions, skipped tests, relaxed expectations, and CI checks that stop failing. ```diff - assert total == 105.3 + assert total > 0 ``` The new assertion accepts many incorrect totals. checkwash can flag changes like this for review, including changes written by coding agents. **Runs locally. No LLM. No network during analysis. Never executes your code.** The install commands below use v0.10.0, the latest published release; 0.11 is unreleased on main ([release history](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/releases/README.md)). Start in one of three ways, each below: Claude Code hooks, the CLI on a repository, or the GitHub Action as a required check. ## Use it with Claude Code You need **Python 3.11+, Git and Claude Code**. Install the CLI, then run the hook installer from the root of your repository: ```bash pipx install checkwash==0.10.0 checkwash hook install --agent claude-code --local ``` This writes checkwash's hooks to `.claude/settings.local.json`, the machine-local Claude Code settings. - The **Stop hook** checks the working tree against HEAD when Claude is about to stop. On a blocking finding it blocks the stop and gives Claude the finding. A SessionStart hook in the same file records where each session starts, so the Stop hook also checks what the session commits. - From 0.11 (unreleased), a local install also adds a **PreToolUse ask**. When an Edit, Write or MultiEdit of a Python test file would leave a finding of one of five weakening rules (`ASSERT_WEAKENED`, `ASSERT_REMOVED`, `TEST_DISABLED`, `TOLERANCE_LOOSENED` and `BROAD_EXCEPT_ADDED`) at high, the hook asks you before the edit is made. In a `claude -p` run nobody can answer, so such an edit is denied; the interactive prompt is not verified in any mode. From 0.11 a local install is the default, and `--shared` writes `.claude/settings.json` with no PreToolUse ask. Both hooks are author-side checks. An edit made through Bash never reaches the ask. When the Stop hook cannot analyse a change, it says so and does not block the stop, except for a changed file over the size limit (see "Know the limits"). Neither hook can stop someone else's merge: the required check under "Use it in CI" is the gate. The 0.11 hooks' limits are in the [0.11 known issues](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-next.md). ## Try it on a repository You need **Python 3.11+ and Git**. Download and try the offline examples first. Windows PowerShell (including 5.1): ```powershell curl.exe -LO https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/releases/download/v0.10.0/checkwash.pyz python checkwash.pyz --version python checkwash.pyz demo ``` PowerShell 5.1 aliases `curl` to `Invoke-WebRequest`; use `curl.exe` as written. macOS/Linux or Git Bash: ```bash curl -LO https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/releases/download/v0.10.0/checkwash.pyz python checkwash.pyz --version python checkwash.pyz demo ``` Then, from the root of a repository with at least two commits: ```bash python checkwash.pyz check HEAD~1..HEAD ``` This checks your last commit. Start with a change you already understand. You can also [download the file in your browser](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/releases/download/v0.10.0/checkwash.pyz). For uncommitted changes use `python checkwash.pyz check`. For a branch review, use `python checkwash.pyz check BASE...HEAD` to compare from the merge base; `BASE..HEAD` compares the two named snapshots directly. From a subdirectory, `check` analyses the whole repository from its Git root and says so in one line on stderr (since v0.8.0, [#416](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/416)). Before v0.8.0, run it from the repository root. For JSON/SARIF output and more examples, see the [embedding guide](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/embedding.md) and the [stability contracts](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/stability.md). ## Use it in CI To stop a merge, make the **`checkwash` status check required** in your repository's branch rules. Installing the tool or adding a workflow alone does not enforce its verdict. Save this as `.github/workflows/checkwash.yml`: ```yaml # .github/workflows/checkwash.yml on: [pull_request] permissions: contents: read jobs: checkwash: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1 with: fetch-depth: 0 persist-credentials: false - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0 with: python-version: "3.12" - uses: taipei49314/checkwash/action@100699796d942af30644738ffbcd1f1c939411c5 # v0.10.0 ``` After the workflow runs, open **Settings → Rules → Rulesets** and require the `checkwash` status context. Keep the job unconditional. If you administer the repository and have this project's ruleset file, you can instead create the rule with: ```bash gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/rulesets --method POST --input action/required-ruleset.json ``` This adds a ruleset; it does not replace existing ones. `checkwash doctor` can inspect the local workflow, but cannot verify live branch protection. The published 0.10.0 CLI's `doctor` accepts only the Action pin built into it, v0.9.0's, so it reports the v0.10.0 pin above as an unsupported SHA ("workflow analysis incomplete", exit 1); `doctor` from this repository's main accepts it. ## When checkwash blocks | Result | What to do | |---|---| | **Pass · exit 0** | No finding requires blocking under your configuration. Keep running your normal tests and review. | | **Block · exit 1** | Read the finding and the diff. It may be weakened verification or a false positive. | | **Error · exit 2** | Resolve the input or analysis error before relying on the result. | The default threshold is **high**: a visible **warn** can still pass. **Read the finding.** Each finding names its rule, its severity, and the file and test it is in. If the change at the top is the whole diff, made in `test_invoice_total` in `tests/test_billing.py`, the finding reads: ```text ASSERT_WEAKENED HIGH tests/test_billing.py :: test_invoice_total test_invoice_total: assertion strength EXACT_VALUE(90) -> BOUND(40) why high: NO_PROD_CHANGE_IN_DIFF no de-escalator applied before assert total == 105.3 after assert total > 0 ``` `EXACT_VALUE(90) -> BOUND(40)` ranks the assertion's strength before and after; 90 is not the value the test expected. `why high` names what raised the finding: here the diff changes no production file, so no production change explains the weaker test. `checkwash check --format json` gives the same findings as JSON. **Fix the change, or record a reviewed exemption.** If the test was weakened by mistake, restore it, and fix the code if the restored test fails. If the weaker test is intended, the report also prints a `checkwash allow` command with the finding's fingerprint, and the ledger file to commit: ```bash checkwash allow "" --reason "why the weaker test is correct" ``` Configuration and exemptions are read from the base side of the diff, so a change cannot exempt itself: commit the entry through review, and it applies to the next diff once it is on the base. Since v0.10.0, a newly winning `.checkwash` config or allowance is compared with its BASE `.greenwash` predecessor, so a change cannot approve its own relaxation either. An entry needs a reason and expires after 90 days by default, 180 at most. Keep `.checkwash/` and `.greenwash/` behind [code owners](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/enterprise.md#4-codeowners). From 0.11 (unreleased), the Stop hook tells Claude not to add an exemption itself but to tell you which finding blocks and why, and the PreToolUse ask asks you to approve only if the weaker test is intended. [Exemption rules](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/enterprise.md#3-allowlist--reviewed-time-boxed-base-side) **Report a false block.** If the change is honest and checkwash blocks it, look for it in the [failure ledger](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/benchmarks/FAILURES.md) first, then open an [issue](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues) with the **checkwash blocked honest work** template, giving the diff and the `checkwash check --format json` output. A report becomes a regression fixture, and the ledger credits the reporter. ## Know the limits **v0.10.0 is alpha.** A pass does not prove that a change is correct or honest. Python is the main language supported; JS/TS support covers a limited set of test patterns. Known gaps remain. An edit that changes nothing, such as `+ 0` in a function a test calls or one line in a template or `AUTHORS`, can still hold a weakened Python or JS/TS test at warn, which passes at the default threshold. #419 is closed as a documented residual, not fixed ([what still passes and how to block it](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/enterprise.md#7-hardening-against-bought-repair-evidence-419)). Read the [versioned known issues](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-v0.10.0.md) and the [earlier limits they build on](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-next.md) before relying on a pass. `REPAIR_EVIDENCE` describes related changes in the same diff; it does not prove a repair is correct, and an edit that changes nothing can earn it (#419). To block such changes, set the Action's `fail-on: warn` (`checkwash doctor` then reports "workflow analysis incomplete" and exits 1, which is expected: it proves only a checkwash step with no `with:`), or run `checkwash check --task` in a CLI step of your own with a base-side `oracle_freeze` contract (the Action has no task input); both block more honest changes too. From 0.11 (unreleased), on a local hook install, the Claude Code PreToolUse hook asks before an Edit, Write or MultiEdit of a Python test leaves a finding of its five weakening rules at high, whatever repair evidence the rest of the working tree holds; its limits are in the [0.11 known issues](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-next.md). In v0.8.0, JS/TS `test.each`, `it.each` and `test.for` tables are not scanned: an assertion weakened or deleted in one, an edited row or a deleted table passes. In v0.9.0, each such table is a test unit, and its rows are read when they can be counted (an inline array or a tagged template, or a same-file `const` read only as a table). The rows of a `describe.each` table stay unread, and a table with a computed title is not a unit ([#428](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/428)). Legitimate refactors can be flagged. The frozen historical corpus records **22 blocks out of 60 (36.7%)**. A separate pre-release source replay records 4/60 blocks, including 2/57 strictly qualified cases; three existing fixture errors remain. These are selected examples, not a general false-positive rate. The v0.10.0 ledger retains 6/60 static source blocks after the [D-185 dispositions](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/oracle-context-dispositions-0.10.0.md), including two additional known legitimate-refactor false blocks. This is a later source readback, not a rewrite of the historical runtime results. A changed file over 1,000,000 bytes is not read. An image, data file, lockfile, document or non-Python production source that large is reported on stderr and earns no repair evidence.
Which files over the limit stop the run, and how each output and the Stop hook report them Since v0.9.0 ([#454](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/454)), `--format json` also lists it under `unread`, SARIF names it in a tool execution notification, and the term report adds a `!` line and, when there is no finding, opens with "analysis incomplete"; the Stop hook's JSON and `--emit-ir` do not name it. A file a detector must read (test, conftest, CI, guardrail, snapshot, JS setup, runner script or test-command file) that large stops the run with exit 2, naming it. So do a `.py` module that large, whether added, deleted, renamed or edited, and a pytest configuration file (`pytest.ini`, `.pytest.ini`, `pytest.toml`, `.pytest.toml`, `tox.ini`, `setup.cfg`, `pyproject.toml`) at any depth: either can change the module a test's import resolves to. So do any non-generated file under the root `scripts/` directory, read for the pytest commands it runs, and any other changed file that large the analysis needs as context. A shell shebang gives a file the shape of a runner script, whatever its name, except a `.py` module or a JS/TS test file. Since v0.9.0 ([#455](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/455)), checkwash reads the first 200 bytes of a side over the limit to tell, and uses them for nothing else; a Git side is streamed and checked against its object id. Where those bytes are read, a file that large whose side starts with a shell shebang stops the run, naming that side, whatever its suffix (a `.py` module or a JS/TS test file that large stops the run anyway, by its own rule). A file with no extension (a dotfile such as `.envrc` counts) without one, such as a `README` or a `LICENSE`, is set aside like any document, unless another rule above makes it one a detector must read. v0.8.0 reads no byte of such a side, so every file with no extension that large stops the run there. In v0.9.0 a Git side over 64,000,000 bytes is not streamed, so its first bytes are not known: a file with no extension still stops the run when one of its Git sides is that large, and a suffixed file whose shebang is only on such a side is still set aside. When a file that large stops the run, since v0.9.0 `--format json` prints `{"unread": [...]}` on stdout instead of nothing: one `unread` entry, for the side the run refused. It is not a findings document, and term and SARIF output stay empty. With a range, json output stays empty too when the refused file is a symlinked pytest configuration's target that no detector must read. Generated output (`build/`, `dist/`, `node_modules/` and the like) is set aside like a production source unless it is a Python module, a pytest configuration, a CI file, a runner script or a file with no extension whose shebang is not known. A root `poetry.lock` or `uv.lock` that large at the base is skipped with a note on stderr, and the skip is not listed under `unread`; when the diff also changes that lockfile, the change's sides over the limit are listed like any other. A root `pyproject.toml` or `requirements*.txt` that large at the base stops every run, naming it: term, json and SARIF output exit 2 and name it on stderr only. The Claude Code Stop hook (`--format hook-json`) reports an engine error, this one included, as a non-blocking "not analysed" message on stdout that quotes the error, and exits 0. Since v0.9.0, when the run stops on a file the hook's diff changes and that file's working-tree side is over the limit, the hook blocks the stop instead, naming the file and asking to shrink, split or revert it ([#456](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/456)). A file whose base side alone is over the limit, a root manifest over it at the base, and a padded file committed before the stop keep the message; the full list is in [subject integrity](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/subject-integrity.md).
Try it on your own changes before making it required. [Coverage and limitations](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/stability.md#coverage-and-adoption-cost) · [Known gaps](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/adversarial-catalog-2026-09.md) ## CI details: doctor and the pin The recommended Action and the CLI above are both **v0.10.0**. Record which version you use. [Full setup and exemptions](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/enterprise.md) **Development snapshots:** the source in this checkout may be newer than the published CLI. [The advertised-release manifest](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/release/advertised.toml) records the version, commit and download bytes behind the installation commands above. New changes require their own candidate evidence and remain unreleased until the publication record verifies them; candidate CI success does not mean that the recommended Action pin includes them. **Advisory: Action trust boundary.** Every published Action release up to and including v0.7.0 runs `python -m pip` and then `checkwash` with the pull request's checkout as the working directory, so a module in that checkout (for example a top-level `pip` package) can replace the installer and then the checker, and the pull request can tamper with the result it is judged by. Under checkwash's threat model that applies to every pull request it judges. v0.8.0 fixes it ([#372](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/pull/372)); pin the v0.10.0 Action above. If you stay on v0.7.0 or earlier, treat a pass as advisory, review the pull request before merging and keep `comment-pr` off. [Known issue](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/SECURITY.md#known-issue-action-trust-boundary) **Which commit is the recommended pin?** A release cannot embed its own commit SHA. Up to v0.10.0, the recommended pin is the commit the tag points to: `git rev-parse 'vX.Y.Z^{commit}'`. From v0.11.0 (D-194), it is the release's Action commit, the tag's second parent's parent: `git rev-parse 'vX.Y.Z^2^1'`. It is not the commit the tag points to. The release pull request's last commit changes one line, `doctor`'s own Action pin, to that Action commit, and the tag differs from the Action commit only in that line. The Action runs only `checkwash check`, which does not import `doctor`. From v0.11.0, a release's `doctor` accepts two Action pins: the one recommended before the release and the release's own Action commit. Pin updaters such as Dependabot and Renovate follow the `# vX.Y.Z` comment, so they will propose the tag's commit, which `doctor` rejects (inferred from those tools' documentation, not run). For the same reason zizmor's `ref-version-mismatch` audit can report the comment (inferred, not run). The Action itself is unaffected: it runs the same check at either commit. `doctor` 0.10.0 does not accept the 0.11.0 pin, so upgrade the CLI and its local hooks first, then the Action pin. The recommended v0.10.0 Action includes the engine published on 2026-10-28 Asia/Taipei. A CLI upgrade does not update an existing Action. [Action reference](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/action/README.md) ## More options and evidence
Install as a CLI or try the included examples If you already use pipx, install the fixed version: ```bash pipx install checkwash==0.10.0 # or from the release tag: pipx install git+https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash@v0.10.0 checkwash check HEAD~1..HEAD checkwash demo # 8 real tampering cases, blocked, offline ``` `checkwash demo` replays eight real tampering cases and one honest fix. It illustrates known patterns; it is not a coverage guarantee. You can run the same examples with `python checkwash.pyz demo`.
Read the measurements and their limits The historical six-repo sweep recorded **46 / 1800 = 2.56%** blocks: **31 false positives (1.72%)**, 15 legitimate policy blocks (0.83%). The tracked artifacts record engine **v0.3.0** (the release commit, swept 2026-09-07) on a corpus used to tune the detectors, not a held-out result. **1.33% of the corpus (24/1800) records opaque production changes**. That flag does not establish that each verdict changed or each diff was unanalyzed. Review methods vary: the three-rater agreement study covers an older 35-diff cohort, not all 46 blocks. The dedicated **22/60 refactor** result (`benchmarks/refactors/results-latest.json`, a dated v0.3.1 snapshot) is a separate population; the general-commit rate does not predict it. [Measurements and source data](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/benchmarks/README.md) · [Generated results](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/benchmarks/RESULTS.md) · [Failure ledger](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/benchmarks/FAILURES.md)
